overall: Atlanta is experiencing a sunny, breezy afternoon with northwest winds near 16 mph (post-frontal pattern) that have brought drier air — dewpoints have dropped from near 72°F overnight to 64°F by early afternoon. Temperatures climbed steadily through the morning and peaked at approximately 13:19 ET at a running max of 84.2°F, already exceeding the NWS forecast high of ~83°F. The 30-minute velocity of -3.6°F/hr strongly suggests the diurnal peak has already passed, and the day is now trending cooler.
forecast_obs_notes: All three NWP models (ECMWF=82.3°F, HRRR=82.6°F, NBM=82.6°F) undershot today's observed high — the running max of 84.2°F has surpassed every model guidance value. The META fused model has responded by concentrating 46.1% of probability mass in the 84–85°F bucket, with a secondary mode at 86–87°F (29.5%), though the intraday obs-driven model independently anchors at 84–85°F (37.5%), lending strong cross-model agreement around the current running max level.
max_temp_prediction: With the running max locked in at 84.2°F, the hour of max already behind us at 13:19 ET, sharply negative 30-minute velocity (-3.6°F/hr), and northwest winds continuing to advect cooler, drier air, the daily TMAX has almost certainly been set. Barring an unexpected late-afternoon convective or dynamic warming pulse — unlikely given current clear-to-scattered skies and the post-frontal wind regime — TMAX should finalize in the 84–85°F range, very close to the observed 84.2°F peak. Confidence is high; the primary risk is a modest upward extension to ~84.5–85°F if scattered cloud breaks temporarily concentrate solar input.
